title.zh: 卷16 列傳第8 趙貴 獨孤信 侯莫陳崇 十二大將軍
title.en: Volume 16 Biographies 8: Zhao Gui; Du Guxin; Houmo Chencheng; 12 Senior Generals
title.raw: 卷16 列傳第8 趙貴 獨孤信 侯莫陳崇 十二大將軍 Volume 16 Biographies 8: Zhao Gui; Du Guxin; Houmo Chencheng; 12 Senior Generals

sentences.zh: 趙貴 獨孤信 侯莫陳崇

translations.literal: Zhao Gui; Du Guxin; Houmo Chen Chong
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui — Du Guxin — Houmo Chen Chong

sentences.zh: 趙貴字元貴，天水南安人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Gui, styled Yuangui, was a native of Nan'an in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui, styled Yuangui, came from Nan'an in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖達，魏庫部尚書、臨晉子。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Da was Wei Minister of the Treasury and Marquis of Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Da had served as Wei minister of the treasury and held the title Marquis of Linjin.

sentences.zh: 祖仁，以良家子鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ren, as a good-household youth, garrisoned Wuchuan and settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ren, posted to Wuchuan as a soldier of good family, made the town his home.

sentences.zh: 貴少穎悟，有節槩。

translations.literal: Gui from youth was keen and perceptive and possessed integrity and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui was bright and quick-minded from boyhood, with a strong sense of honor.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌中，天下兵起，貴率鄉里避難南遷。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, when warfare rose throughout the realm, Gui led his township and neighbors south in flight to escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaochang's reign, as war spread across the land, Zhao Gui led his neighbors south to escape the fighting.

sentences.zh: 屬葛榮陷中山，遂被拘逼。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong took Zhongshan, he was thereupon seized and compelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong captured Zhongshan, Zhao Gui was taken and forced into his service.

sentences.zh: 榮敗，爾朱榮以貴為別將，從討元顥有功，賜爵燕樂縣子，授伏波將軍、武賁中郎將。

translations.literal: When Rong was defeated, Erzhu Rong made Gui a separate commander; following in the campaign against Yuan Hao he had merit, was granted the title Viscount of Yanle county, and was appointed General Who Calms the Waves and Palace Guard Commandant of Martial Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong's defeat Erzhu Rong made Zhao Gui a separate commander; on the campaign against Yuan Hao he earned distinction, received the viscounty of Yanle, and was appointed general who calms the waves and palace guard commandant of martial retainers.

sentences.zh: 從賀拔岳平關中，賜爵魏平縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Following Heba Yue in pacifying Guanzhong, he was granted the title Earl of Weiping county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Heba Yue in pacifying Guanzhong and was enfeoffed Earl of Weiping with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 累遷鎮北將軍、光祿大夫、都督。

translations.literal: By successive promotion he reached General Who Pacifies the North, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to general who pacifies the north, grand master of splendid happiness, and area commander.

sentences.zh: 及岳為侯莫陳悅所害，將吏奔散，莫有守者。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, generals and officials fled and scattered; none remained to hold the line.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue murdered Heba Yue, the officers and staff scattered; no one held the army together.

sentences.zh: 貴謂其黨曰：「吾聞仁義豈有常哉，行之則為君子，違之則為小人。

translations.literal: Gui said to his partisans: "I have heard that benevolence and righteousness—do they have a constant? Practicing them makes one a gentleman; violating them makes one a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui told his followers: "I have heard that benevolence and righteousness are not fixed rules—live by them and you are a gentleman; abandon them and you are a small man.

sentences.zh: 朱伯厚、王叔治感意氣微恩，尚能蹈履名節；

translations.literal: Zhu Bohou and Wang Shuzhi, moved by a slight bond of shared spirit, were still able to tread the path of famed integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bohou and Wang Shuzhi, stirred by the smallest debt of friendship, still kept their names clean;

sentences.zh: 況吾等荷賀拔公國士之遇，寧可自同衆人乎？

translations.literal: How much more we, who received Lord Heba's treatment as men of the state—can we equate ourselves with the common run?"
translations.idiomatic: how much more we, whom Lord Heba treated as men of the realm—can we sink to the level of the crowd?"

sentences.zh: 」涕泣歔欷。

translations.literal: " With tears he wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 於是從之者五十人。

translations.literal: Thereupon fifty men followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty men followed him.

sentences.zh: 乃詣悅詐降，悅信之。

translations.literal: He then went to Yue and feigned surrender; Yue believed him.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Houmochen Yue and pretended to submit; Yue believed him.

sentences.zh: 因請收葬岳，言辭慷慨，悅壯而許之。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested to recover and bury Yue; his words were impassioned, and Yue, admiring him, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to recover Heba Yue's body for burial; his speech was fierce and moving, and Yue, impressed, agreed.

sentences.zh: 貴乃收岳屍還，與寇洛等糾合其衆，奔平涼，共圖拒悅。

translations.literal: Gui then recovered Yue's corpse and returned; with Kou Luo and the others he gathered the host, fled to Pingliang, and together plotted to resist Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui recovered the body and withdrew; with Kou Luo and others he rallied the troops, withdrew to Pingliang, and planned resistance against Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 貴首議迎太祖，語在《太祖紀》。

translations.literal: Gui was first to propose welcoming the Grand Progenitor; the account is in the "Annals of the Grand Progenitor."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui was first to propose welcoming Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai; the account is in the Grand Progenitor's annals.

sentences.zh: 太祖至，以貴為大都督，領府司馬。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor arrived, he made Gui grand commander and concurrent chief clerk of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai arrived, he made Zhao Gui grand commander and chief clerk of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 悅平，以本將軍、持節，行秦州事、當州大都督。

translations.literal: When Yue was pacified, with his existing rank and with full credentials he acted as governor of Qin Province and grand commander of that province.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue was crushed, Zhao Gui kept his rank, received full credentials, and governed Qin Province as its grand commander.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，民吏懷之。

translations.literal: In governing he was pure and quiet; officials and commoners alike cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was calm and clean, and both officials and people held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 齊神武舉兵向洛，使其都督韓軌，進據蒲阪。

translations.literal: Gao Huan raised troops toward Luoyang and sent his area commander Han Gui to advance and seize Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan marched on Luoyang and sent his commander Han Gui to seize Puban.

sentences.zh: 太祖以貴為行臺，與梁禦等討之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor made Gui mobile headquarters and, with Liang Yu and others, campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai made Zhao Gui mobile headquarters commander and, with Liang Yu and others, marched against Han Gui.

sentences.zh: 未濟河而魏孝武已西入關。

translations.literal: Before they had crossed the river, Emperor Xiaowu of Wei had already entered the Pass westward.
translations.idiomatic: Before they crossed the Yellow River, Emperor Xiaowu of Wei had already fled west through the Pass.

sentences.zh: 拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司、兼右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Three Divisions Court Equipage, and concurrent right guard general.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand general of chariots and cavalry with three-division court equipage and concurrent right guard general.

sentences.zh: 時曹泥據靈州拒守，以貴為大都督，與李弼等率衆討之。

translations.literal: At the time Cao Ni held Ling Province in defiance; Gui was made grand commander and, with Li Bi and others, led troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ni was holding out in Ling Province; Zhao Gui was made grand commander and, with Li Bi and others, led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯、增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to marquis and his fief increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis and his fief increased by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又以預立魏文帝勳，進爵為公，增邑通前一千五百戶。

translations.literal: Again, for his share in establishing Emperor Wen of Wei, his rank was advanced to duke and his fief together with the previous total reached one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was further raised to duke for helping establish Emperor Wen of Wei, with a combined fief of one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋授岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 時以軍國多務，藉貴力用，遂不之部。

translations.literal: At the time, because military and state affairs were many and pressing, they relied on Gui's strength and use, and so he did not go to his province.
translations.idiomatic: Military and state business was too urgent to spare him; he never took up the Qi governorship.

sentences.zh: 仍領大丞相府左長史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He still held the post of left chief clerk of the Grand Chancellor's headquarters and was given the additional title of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He remained left chief clerk of the grand chancellor's headquarters and was also made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 梁仚定稱亂河右，以貴為隴西行臺，率衆討破之。

translations.literal: Liang Qiding proclaimed rebellion in the lands west of the Yellow River; Gui was made mobile headquarters of Longxi and led troops to campaign against and break him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qiding rebelled west of the river; Zhao Gui was made Longxi mobile headquarters commander and crushed him.

sentences.zh: 從太祖復弘農，戰沙苑，拜侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵中山郡公，除雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Progenitor in recovering Hongnong and fighting at Shaya, he was appointed palace attendant, grand general of fast cavalry, acting three excellencies with court equipage, advanced in rank to Duke of Zhongshan commandery, and made governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in recovering Hongnong and fighting at Shaya, then became palace attendant, grand general of fast cavalry, and acting three excellencies with court equipage; he was raised to Duke of Zhongshan and made governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 從戰河橋，貴與怡峰為左軍，戰不利，先還。

translations.literal: Following in battle at Heqiao, Gui with Yi Feng were the left army; the battle went badly and they returned first.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao Zhao Gui and Yi Feng commanded the left wing; the fight went badly and they withdrew first.

sentences.zh: 又從援玉壁，齊神武遁去。

translations.literal: Again following in relief of Yubi, Gao Huan fled away.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the campaign to relieve Yubi, after which Gao Huan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 高仲密以北豫州降，太祖率師迎之，與東魏人戰於邙山。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongmi surrendered North Yuzhou to them; the Grand Progenitor led troops to welcome him and fought Eastern Wei men at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered North Yuzhou, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched to receive him and fought Eastern Wei at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 貴為左軍，失律，諸軍因此並潰。

translations.literal: Gui was the left army; he lost discipline, and the armies thereupon all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui held the left wing, broke formation, and the whole army collapsed with him.

sentences.zh: 坐免官，以驃騎、大都督領本軍。

translations.literal: By offense he was stripped of office; with the rank of grand general of fast cavalry and as grand commander he continued to lead his original army.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office but kept command of his army as grand general of fast cavalry and grand commander.

sentences.zh: 尋復官爵，拜御史中尉，加大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon his office and enfeoffment were restored; he was appointed censor-in-chief and given the additional rank of grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his titles were restored; he was made censor-in-chief and promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 東魏將高岳、慕容紹宗等圍王思政於潁川，貴率軍援之，東南諸州兵亦受貴節度。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei generals Gao Yue, Murong Shaozong, and others besieged Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan; Gui led an army to relieve him, and the troops of the southeastern provinces also came under Gui's command and control.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei generals Gao Yue and Murong Shaozong besieged Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan; Zhao Gui marched to relieve him, and southeastern provincial forces also fell under his command.

sentences.zh: 東魏人遏洧水灌城，軍不得至，思政遂沒。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei men blocked the Wei River and flooded the city; the army could not arrive, and Sizheng thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy dammed the Wei River and flooded the city; Zhao Gui's army could not reach it, and Wang Sizheng was lost.

sentences.zh: 貴乃班師。

translations.literal: Gui then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋拜柱國〔大〕將軍，賜姓乙弗氏。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Pillar-of-State (Da) [emended: great] General; granted the surname Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand pillar-of-state general and granted the surname Yifu.

sentences.zh: 茹茹寇廣武，貴擊破之，斬首數千級，收其輜重，振旅而還。

translations.literal: The Rouran raided Guangwu; Gui attacked and broke them, beheaded several thousand, seized their baggage train, and returned with the army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided Guangwu, Zhao Gui routed them, took several thousand heads, captured their supply train, and returned in good order.

sentences.zh: 六官建，以貴為太保、大宗伯，改封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, Gui was made grand tutor and grand herald; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Nanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were established, Zhao Gui became grand tutor and grand herald, and his title was changed to Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，遷太傅、大冢宰，進封楚國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was transferred to grand tutor and grand minister of state, advanced in rank to Duke of the State of Chu, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Zhao Gui was made grand tutor and grand minister of state, raised to Duke of Chu with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 初，貴與獨孤信等皆與太祖等夷，及孝閔帝卽位，晉公護攝政，貴自以元勳佐命，每懷怏怏，有不平之色，乃與信謀殺護。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Gui together with Du Guxin and the others were equals with the Grand Progenitor; when Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Duke of Jin Hu held regency, and Gui, considering himself a founding minister who had aided the mandate, constantly harbored discontent and showed an air of grievance; he therefore plotted with Guxin to kill Hu.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhao Gui, Du Guxin, and others had stood as equals of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai; when Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne Yuwen Hu took power as regent, and Zhao Gui—counting himself a founding minister—grew resentful and began plotting with Du Guxin to kill him.

sentences.zh: 及期，貴欲發，信止之。

translations.literal: When the day came, Gui wished to act; Guxin stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived Zhao Gui meant to strike; Du Guxin held him back.

sentences.zh: 尋為開府宇文盛所告，被誅。

translations.literal: Soon he was denounced by Acting Three Excellencies Yuwen Sheng and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuwen Sheng exposed the plot, and Zhao Gui was executed.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信，雲中人也，本名如願。

translations.literal: Du Guxin was a native of Yunzhong; his original name was Ruyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin came from Yunzhong; his birth name was Ruyuan.

sentences.zh: 魏氏之初，有三十六部，其先伏留屯者，為部落大人，與魏俱起。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wei clan, there were thirty-six divisions; his ancestor among those of Fuliu Tun was tribal paramount of the division and rose together with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wei there were thirty-six tribal divisions; his forebear of Fuliu Tun was paramount of his division and rose with the Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖俟尼，和平中，以良家子自雲中鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sini, in the Heping era, as a good-household youth garrisoned Wuchuan from Yunzhong and settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sini, posted from Yunzhong to Wuchuan as a soldier of good family during the Heping era, made the town his home.

sentences.zh: 父庫者，為領民酋長，少雄豪有節義，北州咸敬服之。

translations.literal: His father Kuzhe was a tribal chief commanding the people; from youth he was bold and heroic and possessed integrity and righteousness; all the northern provinces alike respected and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuzhe was a tribal chief; bold, honorable, and fierce from youth, he commanded respect across the north.

sentences.zh: 信美容儀，善騎射。

translations.literal: Guxin had fine looks and bearing and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin was handsome and a fine horseman and archer.

sentences.zh: 正光末，與賀拔度等同斬衛可孤，由是知名。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang, together with Heba Du and others he beheaded Wei Ke'gu, and by this became known.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Zhenguang era he and Heba Du and others killed Wei Ke'gu and won a name for it.

sentences.zh: 以北邊喪亂，避地中山，為葛榮所獲。

translations.literal: Because the northern frontier was in disorder and ruin, he fled to Zhongshan for refuge and was captured by Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern frontier collapsed he took refuge at Zhongshan and was seized by Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 信旣少年，好自修飾，服章有殊於衆，軍中號為獨孤郎。

translations.literal: Guxin being still young, loved to adorn himself; his dress and insignia differed from the multitude, and within the army they called him the Dugu Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin was still young, fastidious about his appearance, and dressed finer than the rest; the army called him the Dugu Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 及爾朱氏破葛榮，以信為別將。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan broke Ge Rong, they made Guxin a separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the Erzhu clan defeated Ge Rong, Du Guxin was made a separate commander.

sentences.zh: 從征韓婁，信疋馬挑戰，擒賊漁陽王袁肆周，以功拜員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Following on campaign against Han Lou, Guxin with one horse challenged to battle and captured the bandit Prince of Yuyang, Yuan Sizhou; for merit he was appointed acting gentleman attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Han Lou, Du Guxin rode out alone to challenge the enemy and captured the rebel Prince of Yuyang, Yuan Sizhou; for this he was made acting gentleman attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋轉驍騎將軍，因鎮滏口。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to general of fierce cavalry; he thereupon garrisoned Fukou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made general of fierce cavalry and garrisoned Fukou.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，榮以信為前驅，與顥黨戰於河北，破之。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao entered Luoyang; Rong made Guxin vanguard and fought Hao's partisans on the north of the river and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Erzhu Rong made Du Guxin vanguard; north of the river he routed Yuan Hao's allies.

sentences.zh: 拜安南將軍，賜爵爰德縣侯。

translations.literal: Appointed General Who Pacifies the South; granted the title Marquis of Yuande county.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who pacifies the south and enfeoffed Marquis of Yuande.

sentences.zh: 建明初，出為荊州新野鎮將，帶新野郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianming, he went out as garrison commander of Xinye in Jing Province, concurrently holding the post of administrator of Xinye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianming era he went out as garrison commander of Xinye in Jing Province and concurrently administered Xinye commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋遷荊州防城大都督，帶南鄉守。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to grand commander for defense of the city in Jing Province, concurrently holding the post of administrator of Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Jing Province's grand commander for city defense and concurrently administrator of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 頻典二部，皆有聲績。

translations.literal: Repeatedly administering two departments, in each case he had reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He held two posts in succession, and in each earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝出鎮荊州，乃表信為大都督。

translations.literal: Heba Sheng went out to garrison Jing Province and thereupon memorialized the throne to make Guxin grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Sheng took up the Jing Province garrison, he recommended Du Guxin as grand commander.

sentences.zh: 從勝攻梁下溠戍，破之，遷武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Following Sheng in attacking Liang's Xiasao garrison, he broke it and was transferred to martial guard general.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Heba Sheng against Liang's Xiasao garrison, took it, and was promoted to martial guard general.

sentences.zh: 及勝弟岳為侯莫陳悅所害，勝乃令信入關，撫岳餘衆。

translations.literal: When Sheng's younger brother Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Sheng then ordered Guxin to enter the Pass and pacify Yue's remaining host.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Sheng's brother Heba Yue, Sheng sent Du Guxin through the Pass to rally Yue's remaining troops.

sentences.zh: 屬太祖已統岳兵，信與太祖鄉里，少相友善，相見甚歡。

translations.literal: As the Grand Progenitor had already taken command of Yue's army, Guxin and the Grand Progenitor were townsmen; from youth they had been somewhat friendly, and when they met they were very glad.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had already taken over Heba Yue's army; he and Du Guxin were from the same home country and had been friends since youth, and their meeting was warm.

sentences.zh: 因令信入洛請事，至雍州，大使元毗又遣信還荊州。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Guxin to enter Luoyang to report on affairs; when he reached Yong Province, the grand envoy Yuan Pi again sent Guxin back to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai then sent Du Guxin to Luoyang on business; at Yong Province the grand envoy Yuan Pi sent him back to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 尋徵信入朝，魏孝武雅相委任。

translations.literal: Soon Guxin was summoned to court; Emperor Xiaowu of Wei greatly entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin was soon recalled to court, and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei relied on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，事起倉卒，信單騎及之於瀍澗。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu moved west, the affair arose in sudden haste; Guxin with a single horse caught up with him at Chan Stream.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west the crisis came in an instant; Du Guxin rode alone and caught up with him at Chan Stream.

sentences.zh: 孝武歎曰：「武衛遂能辭父母，捐妻子，遠來從我。

translations.literal: Xiaowu sighed and said: "The martial guard can indeed leave parents, abandon wife and children, and come from afar to follow me.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu sighed and said: "The martial guard can leave parents, abandon wife and children, and ride from afar to follow me.

sentences.zh: 世亂識貞良，豈虛言哉。

translations.literal: In chaotic times one knows the loyal and good—was that an empty saying?"
translations.idiomatic: In chaos one learns who is true—those were not empty words."

sentences.zh: 」卽賜信御馬一疋，進爵浮陽郡公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He thereupon granted Guxin one imperial horse and advanced his rank to Duke of Fuyang commandery, fief one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Du Guxin one of the imperial horses and raised him to Duke of Fuyang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時荊州雖陷東魏，民心猶戀本朝。

translations.literal: At the time, although Jing Province had fallen to Eastern Wei, the hearts of the people still clung to the original court.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jing Province had fallen to Eastern Wei, the people still looked to the old court.

sentences.zh: 乃以信為衛大將軍、都督三荊州諸軍事，兼尚書右僕射、東南道行臺、大都督、荊州刺史以招懷之。

translations.literal: Guxin was therefore made grand general of the guard, commander of all military affairs of the three Jing provinces, concurrently right vice-minister of the Masters of Writing, mobile headquarters of the southeast route, grand commander, and governor of Jing Province to summon and cherish them.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin was therefore made grand general of the guard, commander of the three Jing provinces, concurrent right vice-minister of the Masters of Writing, southeast-route mobile headquarters commander, grand commander, and governor of Jing Province to win them back.

sentences.zh: 信至武陶，東魏遣其弘農郡守田八能，率蠻左之衆，拒信于淅陽；

translations.literal: When Guxin reached Wutao, Eastern Wei sent its administrator of Hongnong commandery Tian Baneng to lead the tribes of the southern barbarians and resist Guxin at Xiyang;
translations.idiomatic: When Du Guxin reached Wutao, Eastern Wei sent Tian Baneng, administrator of Hongnong, with southern tribal forces to block him at Xiyang;

sentences.zh: 又遣其都督張齊民，以步騎三千出信之後。

translations.literal: again they sent their area commander Zhang Qimin with three thousand infantry and cavalry to emerge behind Guxin.
translations.idiomatic: and sent Zhang Qimin with three thousand foot and horse to strike from the rear.

sentences.zh: 信謂其衆曰：「今我士卒不滿千人，而首尾受敵。

translations.literal: Guxin said to his host: "Now my officers and soldiers are fewer than one thousand, yet front and rear we receive the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin told his men: "We have fewer than a thousand soldiers and enemies before and behind us.

sentences.zh: 若卻擊齊民，則敵人謂為退走，必來要截。

translations.literal: If we turn and strike Qimin, the enemy will take it as retreat and flight and will surely come to intercept and cut us off.
translations.idiomatic: If we turn on Qimin, they will read it as retreat and cut us off.

sentences.zh: 未若先破八能。

translations.literal: Better first to break Baneng."
translations.idiomatic: Better break Baneng first."

sentences.zh: 」遂奮擊，八能敗而齊民亦潰。

translations.literal: He thereupon struck with force; Baneng was defeated and Qimin also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked at once; Baneng was routed and Qimin's force collapsed with him.

sentences.zh: 信乘勝襲荊州。

translations.literal: Guxin, riding victory, raided Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin pressed the victory and swept into Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 東魏刺史辛纂勒兵出戰。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's governor Xin Zuan drew up troops and went out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's governor Xin Zuan marched out to fight.

sentences.zh: 士庶旣懷信遺惠，信臨陣喻之，莫不解體。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners, having already cherished Guxin's lingering kindness, when Guxin faced the battle line and addressed them, none failed to melt.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people already owed Du Guxin their loyalty; when he spoke to them from the front, their will to resist melted away.

sentences.zh: 因而縱兵擊之，纂大敗，奔城趨門，未及闔，信都督楊忠等前驅斬纂。

translations.literal: He thereupon released troops to strike them; Zuan was greatly defeated, fled toward the city gate, and before it could be shut, Guxin's area commander Yang Zhong and others as vanguard beheaded Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then unleashed his troops; Xin Zuan was routed, ran for the gate, and before it could close Yang Zhong and the vanguard cut him down.

sentences.zh: 語在《忠傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Zhong."
translations.idiomatic: The account is in Yang Zhong's biography.

sentences.zh: 於是三荊遂定。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three Jing provinces were settled.
translations.idiomatic: The three Jing provinces were thus secured.

sentences.zh: 就拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Three Divisions Court Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made grand general of chariots and cavalry with three-division court equipage.

sentences.zh: 東魏又遣其將高敖曹、侯景等率衆奄至。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei again sent its generals Gao Aocao, Hou Jing, and others to lead troops arriving in sudden force.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Gao Aocao, Hou Jing, and others with a sudden assault force.

sentences.zh: 信以衆寡不敵，遂率麾下奔梁。

translations.literal: Guxin, because the many were no match for the few, thereupon led his personal followers and fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Du Guxin led his personal followers and fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 居三載，梁武帝方始許信還北。

translations.literal: After dwelling three years, Emperor Wu of Liang at last permitted Guxin to return north.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in Liang, Emperor Wu of Liang at last allowed Du Guxin to return north.

sentences.zh: 信父母旣在山東，梁武帝問信所往，信答以事君無二。

translations.literal: Guxin's parents were already in Shandong; Emperor Wu of Liang asked Guxin where he was going, and Guxin answered that in serving one's lord there is no second [allegiance].
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin's parents were in Shandong; when Emperor Wu asked where he meant to go, Du Guxin answered that a subject serves one lord only.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝深義之，禮送甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang deeply approved his righteousness and sent him off with great courtesy and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu admired his loyalty and sent him north with rich honors.

sentences.zh: 大統三年秋，至長安。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Datong, he reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Datong 3 (537) he reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 自以虧損國威，上書謝罪。

translations.literal: Considering himself to have diminished the state's prestige, he submitted a memorial apologizing for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he had shamed the state, he wrote to apologize for his failure.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝付尚書議之，七兵尚書、陳郡王

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei handed the matter to the Masters of Writing for deliberation—the Minister of the Seven Armies, Prince of Chen commandery
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei referred the matter to the Masters of Writing—the Minister of the Seven Armies, Prince of Chen commandery

sentences.zh: （王言）

translations.literal: (Wang Yan)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Wang Yan]

sentences.zh: 〔玄〕等議，以為「邊將董戎，龔行天罰，喪師敗績，國刑無舍。

translations.literal: [Xuan] and others deliberated, saying: "Frontier generals who marshal troops and carry Heaven's punishment—when they lose the army and fail in the campaign, the state punishment allows no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and others deliberated, saying: "Frontier generals who bear Heaven's mandate to chastise wrongdoers and yet lose their armies—the law knows no mercy.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史獨孤如願，任當推轂，遠襲襄、宛，斬賊帥辛纂，傳首京師，論功語效，寔合嘉賞。

translations.literal: Jing Province governor Dugu Ruyuan, his charge being to push the chariot, made a distant raid on Xiang and Wan, beheaded the bandit chief Xin Zuan, and sent his head to the capital; in reckoning merit and speaking of achievement, he truly deserved fine reward.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province governor Du Guxin, entrusted with full command, had raided deep into Xiang and Wan, beheaded the rebel leader Xin Zuan, and sent his head to the capital—a feat that plainly merited reward.

sentences.zh: 但庸績不終，旋致淪沒，責成之義，朝寄有違。

translations.literal: Yet meritorious deeds were not carried through and he soon fell into ruin; the principle of completing the charge—the court's trust was violated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his success was not sustained and he was soon lost; by the rule that a commission must be fulfilled, he had failed the court's trust.

sentences.zh: 然孤軍數千，後援未接，賊衆我寡，難以自固。

translations.literal: Still, a lone army of several thousand with rear support not yet joined—bandits many, we few—it was hard to hold firm on one's own.
translations.idiomatic: Still, he had only a few thousand men with no reinforcements, outnumbered and unable to stand alone.

sentences.zh: 旣經恩降，理絕刑書。

translations.literal: Since grace in reduction of punishment had already been granted, reason excludes the criminal code.
translations.idiomatic: Grace had already been shown him, so the penal code no longer applied.

sentences.zh: 昔秦宥孟明，漢舍廣利，卒能改過立功，垂芳竹帛。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin pardoned Meng Ming and Han spared Guangli; in the end they were able to reform their faults and establish merit, leaving fragrance in the bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Qin once spared Meng Ming and Han forgave Li Guangli; both went on to redeem themselves and win lasting fame.

sentences.zh: 以今方古，抑有成規。

translations.literal: Measuring the present against antiquity, there is indeed an established rule.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing present with past, there was clear precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，請赦罪，復其舊職」。

translations.literal: We your ministers jointly deliberate: we request pardon of the offense and restoration to his former office."
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers therefore ask that his offense be pardoned and his former office restored."

sentences.zh: 魏文帝詔曰：「如願荊、襄之役，寔展功效。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei decreed: "Ruyuan's Jing and Xiang campaign truly displayed achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei decreed: "Du Guxin's campaign in Jing and Xiang did show real service.

sentences.zh: 旣屬強寇，力屈道窮，歸賊不可，還朝路絕，適事求宜，未足稱過。

translations.literal: Having encountered a strong foe, his strength bent and the way was exhausted; to return to the bandits was impossible and the road back to court was cut off—seeking what suited the affair, it is insufficient to call it fault.
translations.idiomatic: He met a powerful enemy, was spent, and could neither submit to the foe nor find a way home—given the circumstances, he can hardly be blamed.

sentences.zh: 違難如吳，誠貫夷險，義全終始，良可嘉歎。

translations.literal: Enduring hardship like Wu, his sincerity penetrating easy and perilous, his righteousness complete from beginning to end—truly worthy of praise and sighing admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He bore hardship through every danger with constancy from first to last—truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 復情存謙退，款心謝責。

translations.literal: Again, his feeling preserved humility and withdrawal; with sincere heart he declined blame.
translations.idiomatic: He had shown humility and offered a sincere apology.

sentences.zh: 甯容議及恩降，止雲免咎，斯則事失權宜，理乖通變。

translations.literal: How could one allow the deliberation to reach only to grace in reduction of punishment and stop at saying merely exemption from blame? That then is the affair losing what suits the moment and reason departing from flexible change.
translations.idiomatic: To treat this as no more than a pardon from punishment falls short of what the moment requires.

sentences.zh: 可轉驃騎大將軍，加侍中、開府，其使持節、儀同三司、浮陽郡公悉如故。」

translations.literal: He may be transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with the added posts of attendant-in-ordinary and opening-the-feudatory; his bearer of the staff, three-division court equipage, and Duke of Fuyang commandery shall all remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be made grand general of agile cavalry, with attendant-in-ordinary and opening-the-feudatory added; his staff, three-division court equipage, and ducal title of Fuyang shall all stand as before."

sentences.zh: 尋拜領軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed commander of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of the guard.

sentences.zh: 仍從太祖復弘農，破沙苑。

translations.literal: He still followed the Grand Progenitor in recovering Hongnong and breaking Shaya.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in recovering Hongnong and winning at Shaya.

sentences.zh: 改封河內郡公，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Henei commandery; his fief was increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Duke of Henei and his fief increased by two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時俘虜中有信親屬，始得父凶問，乃發喪行服。

translations.literal: At the time among the captives were Guxin's close kin; he first received word of his father's death and thereupon began mourning and wore mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: Among the prisoners were Du Guxin's kinsmen; from them he first learned of his father's death and went into mourning.

sentences.zh: 尋起為大都督，率衆與馮翊王元季海入洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised up as grand commander and led troops with Prince of Fengyi Yuan Jihai into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to serve as grand commander and entered Luoyang with Prince of Fengyi Yuan Jihai at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 潁、豫、襄、廣、陳留之地，竝相繼款附。

translations.literal: The lands of Ying, Yu, Xiang, Guang, and Chenliu all in succession came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Yu, Xiang, Guang, and Chenliu submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 四年，東魏將侯景等率衆圍洛陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Eastern Wei generals Hou Jing and others led troops to besiege Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Hou Jing and other Eastern Wei generals besieged Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 信據金墉城，隨方拒守，旬有餘日。

translations.literal: Xin held Jinyong city and, according to each direction, resisted and defended—for ten-plus days.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin held Jinyong and beat back attacks from every side for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 及太祖至瀍東，景等退走。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor reached the east of Chan, Jing and the others withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai reached the east bank of the Chan, Hou Jing and the others withdrew.

sentences.zh: 信與李遠為右軍，戰不利，東魏遂有洛陽。

translations.literal: Xin together with Li Yuan were the right army; the battle went badly and Eastern Wei thereupon held Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin and Li Yuan commanded the right wing; the fight went badly and Eastern Wei took Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 六年，侯景寇荊州，太祖令信與李弼出武關。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Hou Jing raided Jing Province; the Grand Progenitor ordered Xin together with Li Bi to go out through Wu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hou Jing raided Jing Province; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent Du Guxin and Li Bi out through Wu Pass.

sentences.zh: 景退，以信為大使，慰撫三荊。

translations.literal: When Jing withdrew, Xin was made grand envoy to comfort and pacify the three Jing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing withdrew, Du Guxin was made grand envoy to reassure the three Jing provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋除隴右十州大都督、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon appointed grand commander of the ten provinces of Longyou and governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed grand commander of the ten Longyou provinces and governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 先是，守宰闇弱，政令乖方，民有冤訟，歷年不能斷決。

translations.literal: Earlier, the guarding officials were dim and weak, government orders deviated from the proper direction, and when the people had grievances and lawsuits, year after year they could not be judged and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the local officials had been weak, policy had gone awry, and lawsuits had piled up unresolved for years.

sentences.zh: 及信在州，事無壅滯。

translations.literal: When Xin was in the province, affairs had no blockage or delay.
translations.idiomatic: Under Du Guxin nothing stalled in the province.

sentences.zh: 示以禮教，勸以耕桑，數年之中，公私富實。

translations.literal: He displayed ritual teaching and encouraged farming and sericulture; within several years, public and private were rich and full.
translations.idiomatic: He taught courtesy and urged farming and silk production; within a few years public and private stores were full.

sentences.zh: 流民願附者數萬家。

translations.literal: Wandering commoners who wished to attach themselves numbered tens of thousands of households.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of refugee families chose to settle under his rule.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其信著遐邇，故賜名為信。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, because his trustworthiness was renowned far and near, therefore granted the name Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, seeing that his trustworthiness was known far and wide, gave him the name Xin ("Trust").

sentences.zh: 七年，岷州刺史、赤水蕃王梁仚定舉兵反，詔信討之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Min Province governor and Chishui barbarian king Liang Xiansheng raised troops in rebellion; an edict ordered Xin to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Liang Xiansheng, king of the Chishui tribes and governor of Min Province, rebelled; an edict sent Du Guxin against him.

sentences.zh: 仚定尋為其部下所殺。

translations.literal: Xiansheng was soon killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Xiansheng was soon killed by his own followers.

sentences.zh: 而仚定子弟，仍收其餘衆。

translations.literal: Yet Xiansheng's sons and younger brothers still gathered his remaining host.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and brothers still held the remnant force together.

sentences.zh: 信乃勒兵向萬年，頓三交口。

translations.literal: Xin thereupon drew up troops toward Wannian and encamped at Sankou Crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin marched on Wannian and encamped at Sankou Crossing.

sentences.zh: 賊並力拒守，信因詭道趨稠松嶺。

translations.literal: The bandits combined strength to resist and defend; Xin by a devious route hastened toward Chousong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed to hold him off; Du Guxin took a hidden route toward Chousong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 賊不虞信兵之至，望風奔潰。

translations.literal: The bandits did not anticipate Xin's troops arriving; at sight of the wind they fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did not expect him; at his approach they broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北，徑至城下，賊並出降。

translations.literal: Riding victory he pursued north, went straight to below the city wall, and the bandits all came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the pursuit to the walls and the rebels surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 加授太子太保。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 邙山之戰，大軍不利。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mount Mang the great army fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang the main army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 信與于謹收散卒自後擊之，齊神武追騎驚擾，諸軍因此得全。

translations.literal: Xin together with Yu Jin gathered scattered soldiers and from the rear struck them; Qi Divine Martial's pursuing horsemen were thrown into alarm and disturbance, and the various armies thereby were saved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin and Yu Jin rallied the broken troops and struck from the rear; Gao Huan's pursuers were thrown into disorder and the army got away intact.

sentences.zh: 十二年，涼州刺史宇文仲和據州不受代，太祖令信率開府怡峯討之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Liang Province governor Yuwen Zhonghe held the province and would not accept replacement; the Grand Progenitor ordered Xin to lead Opening-the-Feudatory Yi Feng to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Yuwen Zhonghe, governor of Liang Province, refused to yield his post; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent Du Guxin with Yi Feng to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 仲和嬰城固守，信夜令諸將以沖梯攻其東北，信親帥壯士襲其西南，值明克之。

translations.literal: Zhonghe shut the city gates and held firm; at night Xin ordered the generals to use scaling ladders to attack the northeast, while Xin personally led stalwart warriors to strike the southwest—at dawn it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe shut himself in the city; by night Du Guxin sent his generals with scaling ladders against the northeast while he himself led picked men against the southwest—the city fell at dawn.

sentences.zh: 擒仲和，虜其民六千戶，送于長安。

translations.literal: He captured Zhonghe, took captive his people six thousand households, and sent them to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zhonghe prisoner, resettled six thousand of his people, and sent them to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 拜大司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 十三年，大軍東討。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the great army marched east to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the main army marched east on campaign.

sentences.zh: 時以茹茹為寇，令信移鎮河陽。

translations.literal: At the time because the Rouran were raiding, Xin was ordered to shift his garrison to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran were raiding at the time, so Du Guxin was ordered to move his garrison to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進位柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year his rank was advanced to Pillar-of-State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to pillar-of-state grand general.

sentences.zh: 錄剋下溠、守洛陽、破岷州、平涼州等功，增封，聽回授諸子。

translations.literal: Recording the merits of capturing Xia, holding Luoyang, breaking Min Province, and pacifying Liang Province, his enfeoffment was increased and he was permitted to transfer fiefs back to his sons.
translations.idiomatic: For taking Xia, holding Luoyang, breaking Min Province, and pacifying Liang Province his fief was increased and he was allowed to pass portions to his sons.

sentences.zh: 於是第二子善封魏寧縣公，第三子穆文侯縣侯，第四子藏義甯縣侯，邑各一千戶；

translations.literal: Thereupon the second son Shan was enfeoffed Duke of Weining county, the third son Mu Viscount of Wenhou county, the fourth son Zang Marquis of Yining county—each fief one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: His second son Shan received Weining county, his third Mu Wenhou county, and his fourth Zang Yining county—each with a fief of one thousand households;

sentences.zh: 第五子順項城縣伯，第六子陀建忠縣伯，邑各五百戶。

translations.literal: the fifth son Shun Baron of Xiangcheng county, the sixth son Tuo Baron of Jianzhong county—each fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: his fifth son Shun Xiangcheng county and his sixth Tuo Jianzhong county—each with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 信在隴右歲久，啟求還朝，太祖不許。

translations.literal: Xin had long been in Longyou; he memorialized requesting return to court, and the Grand Progenitor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin had been in Longyou many years and asked to return to court; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai refused.

sentences.zh: 或有自東魏來者，又告其母凶問，信發喪行服。

translations.literal: Some who came from Eastern Wei again reported word of his mother's death; Xin began mourning and wore mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: Someone arriving from Eastern Wei brought word of his mother's death; Du Guxin went into mourning again.

sentences.zh: 屬魏太子與

translations.literal: It happened that the Wei crown prince and
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Wei crown prince and

translations.literal: (Shi)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Shi]

sentences.zh: 〔太〕祖巡北邊，因至河陽吊信。

translations.literal: [Tai] Zu toured the northern frontier and therefore came to Heyang to condole with Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was touring the northern frontier and came to Heyang to console Du Guxin.

sentences.zh: 信陳哀苦，請終禮制，又不許。

translations.literal: Xin stated his grief and bitterness and requested to complete the rites; again he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin pleaded his grief and asked to finish mourning; again he was refused.

sentences.zh: 於是追贈信父庫者司空公，追封信母費連氏常山郡君。

translations.literal: Thereupon posthumously awarded Xin's father Kuzhe as Duke of Works and posthumously enfeoffed Xin's mother Lady Feilian as Lady of Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made his father Kuzhe duke of works and his mother Lady Feilian Lady of Changshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 十六年，大軍東討，信率隴右數萬人從軍，至崤阪而還。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the great army marched east to attack; Xin led several tens of thousands from Longyou to follow the army, reaching Xiao Pass and returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when the main army marched east, Du Guxin led tens of thousands from Longyou as far as Xiao Pass and then returned.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜大司馬。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were established, he was appointed grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，遷太保、大宗伯，進封衛國公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was transferred to Grand Tutor and Grand Minister of Clan Affairs, advanced in rank to Duke of the State of Wei, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Du Guxin was made grand tutor and grand minister of clan affairs, raised to Duke of Wei with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 趙貴誅後，信以同謀坐免。

translations.literal: After Zhao Gui was executed, Xin on account of shared plotting sat and was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao Gui's execution Du Guxin was dismissed for complicity in the plot.

sentences.zh: 居無幾，晉公護又欲殺之，以其名望素重，不欲顯其罪，逼令自盡於家。

translations.literal: Within not long, Duke of Jin Hu again wished to kill him; because his fame and standing had long been heavy, he did not wish to display his crime and forced him to take his own life at home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu wanted him dead; unwilling to expose the charge against so famous a man, he forced Du Guxin to kill himself at home.

sentences.zh: 時年五十五。

translations.literal: At the time his age was fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 信風度弘雅，有奇謀大略。

translations.literal: Xin's bearing and manner were broad and refined; he had strange stratagems and great designs.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin was magnanimous and elegant, with bold plans and far-reaching designs.

sentences.zh: 太祖初啟霸業，唯有關中之地，以隴右形勝，故委信鎮之。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor first opened the hegemonic enterprise, he had only the lands of Guanzhong; because Longyou was strategically strong, he therefore entrusted Xin to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai first built his power base he held only Guanzhong; because Longyou was strategically vital, he put Du Guxin in charge there.

sentences.zh: 旣為百姓所懷，聲振鄰國。

translations.literal: Having already been cherished by the common people, his reputation shook neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: The people already loved him, and his fame resounded in neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 東魏將侯景之南奔梁也，魏收為檄梁文，矯稱信據隴右不從宇文氏，仍云無關西之憂，欲以威梁人也。

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei general Hou Jing fled south to Liang, Wei Shou wrote a proclamation essay to Liang, falsely claiming that Xin held Longyou and would not follow the Yuwen clan, and further saying there was no worry about Guanxi—intending thereby to overawe the people of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing defected south to Liang, Wei Shou drafted a proclamation to Liang falsely claiming that Du Guxin held Longyou in defiance of the Yuwen house and that the west need not be feared—aiming to intimidate Liang.

sentences.zh: 又信在秦州，嘗因獵日暮，馳馬入城，其帽微側。

translations.literal: Again, when Xin was in Qin Province, once while hunting at day's end he galloped his horse into the city; his cap was slightly askew.
translations.idiomatic: Once while hunting in Qin Province Du Guxin rode into town at dusk with his hat slightly askew.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，而吏民有戴帽者，咸慕信而側帽焉。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, among officials and commoners who wore caps, all admired Xin and tilted their caps accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning every official and townsman who wore a hat copied him and wore it tilted.

sentences.zh: 其為鄰境及士庶所重如此。

translations.literal: That he was so esteemed by neighboring borders and gentry and commoners was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight he carried with neighbors and with officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 善

translations.literal: Shan
translations.idiomatic: Shan

translations.literal: (Zi)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Zi]

sentences.zh: 〔字〕伏陀，幼聰慧，善騎射，以父勳，封魏寧縣公。

translations.literal: [styled] Futu, from youth clever and perceptive, skilled at mounted archery; on account of his father's merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Weining county.
translations.idiomatic: styled Futu, clever from childhood and skilled at riding and archery; for his father's service he was enfeoffed Duke of Weining.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，又以父勳，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，進爵長安郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, again on account of his father's merit he was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Opening-the-Feudatory Three Divisions Court Equipage, with the added post of attendant-in-ordinary, and advanced in rank to Duke of Chang'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei (551) he was again promoted for his father's service to grand general of agile cavalry with opening-the-feudatory three-division court equipage and attendant-in-ordinary, and raised to Duke of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除河州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was appointed governor of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was made governor of He Province.

sentences.zh: 以父負舋，久廢於家。

translations.literal: On account of his father bearing guilt, he was long idle at home.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his father's disgrace he remained at home for years.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，乃授龍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, he was thereupon appointed governor of Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 3 (563) he was appointed governor of Long Province.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，襲爵河內郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe he inherited the title Duke of Henei commandery, fief two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe 6 (569) he succeeded to the ducal title of Henei with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 從高祖東討，以功授上開府。

translations.literal: Following the High Ancestor on the eastern campaign, by merit he was appointed Upper Opening-the-Feudatory.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu on the eastern campaign and was made upper opening-the-feudatory for his service.

sentences.zh: 尋除兗州刺史，政存簡惠，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Soon appointed governor of Yan Province; in government he preserved simplicity and kindness, and the common people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Yan Province; his rule was simple and benevolent, and the people lived securely.

sentences.zh: 卒於位，年三十八。

translations.literal: He died in office; his age was thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、柱國、定趙恆滄瀛五州諸軍事、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded bearer of the staff, pillar-of-state, commander of all military affairs of the five provinces Ding, Zhao, Heng, Cang, and Ying, and governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made bearer of the staff, pillar-of-state, commander over Ding, Zhao, Heng, Cang, and Ying provinces, and governor of Ding.

sentences.zh: 信長女，周明敬后；

translations.literal: Xin's eldest daughter was Empress Mingjing of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin's eldest daughter became Empress Mingjing of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 第四女，元貞皇后；

translations.literal: the fourth daughter, Empress Yuanzhen;
translations.idiomatic: his fourth daughter, Empress Yuanzhen;

sentences.zh: 第七女，隋文獻后。

translations.literal: the seventh daughter, Empress Wenxian of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: and his seventh daughter, Empress Wenxian of Sui.

sentences.zh: 周隋及皇家，三代皆為外戚，自古以來，未之有也。

translations.literal: Zhou, Sui, and the imperial house—for three generations all were maternal kin; from antiquity until now, there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: For three reigns—Northern Zhou, Sui, and the imperial house—his daughters were empresses; nothing like it had ever been seen.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，乃下詔曰：「褒德累行，往代通規；

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he thereupon issued an edict saying: "To praise virtue and accumulate conduct is the common rule of former ages;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne he issued an edict: "To honor virtue and accumulated merit is an ancient rule;

sentences.zh: 追遠慎終，前王盛典。

translations.literal: to pursue the distant and be careful at the end is the former kings' great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: to remember the dead and finish well is a royal duty of old.

sentences.zh: 故使持節、柱國、河內郡開國公信，風宇高曠，獨秀生人，睿哲居宗，清猷映世。

translations.literal: The late bearer of the staff, pillar-of-state, Duke Who Founded the State of Henei commandery Xin—his wind and bearing lofty and wide, alone outstanding among the living, sagely wisdom occupying the ancestral seat, pure plans reflecting on the age.
translations.idiomatic: The late Du Guxin—bearer of the staff, pillar-of-state, and founding duke of Henei—stood above his contemporaries in bearing and wisdom, his clear purpose shining through the age.

sentences.zh: 宏謨長策，道著於弼諧；

translations.literal: Grand designs and long stratagems—his Way was established in assisting harmony;
translations.idiomatic: His great plans and long counsel served the realm in harmony;

sentences.zh: 緯義經仁，事深於拯濟。

translations.literal: weaving righteousness and threading benevolence—his affairs went deep in succoring and relieving.
translations.idiomatic: his weaving of righteousness and benevolence went deep in succoring the people.

sentences.zh: 方當宣風廊廟，亮采臺階，而世屬艱危，功高弗賞。

translations.literal: Just when he should have spread wind in the palace and hall and displayed color on the terrace steps, yet the age belonged to hardship and peril and merit high received no reward.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he should have served prominently at court, the times turned perilous and his high merit went unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 眷言令範，事切於心。

translations.literal: Looking back on his fine model, the affair cuts to the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling his example touches the heart.

sentences.zh: 今景運初開，椒闈肅建。

translations.literal: Now the bright fortune is first opening and the inner quarters are solemnly established.
translations.idiomatic: Now a new fortune opens and the inner palace is duly established.

sentences.zh: 載懷塗山之義，無忘褒紀之典。

translations.literal: We bear in mind the meaning of Tushan and do not forget the canon of honoring records.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of the duty owed at Tushan, we must not neglect the rites of honoring the worthy.

sentences.zh: 可贈太師、上柱國、冀定相滄瀛趙恆洺貝十州諸軍事、冀州刺史，〔封〕趙國公，邑一萬戶。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor, upper pillar-of-state, commander of all military affairs of the ten provinces Ji, Ding, Xiang, Cang, Ying, Zhao, Heng, Mo, Bei, and Ji, and governor of Ji Province, [enfeoff] Duke of Zhao state, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made grand preceptor and upper pillar-of-state, commander over Ji, Ding, Xiang, Cang, Ying, Zhao, Heng, Mo, Bei, and Ji provinces, governor of Ji, and enfeoffed Duke of Zhao with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 諡曰景。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jing (Illustrious).

sentences.zh: 」追贈信父庫者使持節、太尉、上柱國、定恆滄瀛平燕六州諸軍事、定州刺史，封趙國公，邑一萬戶。

translations.literal: " Du Guxin's father Kuzhe was posthumously granted bearer of the staff, Grand Commandant, Superior Pillar of State, Director of military affairs in the six provinces of Ding, Heng, Cang, Ying, Ping, and Yan, and Inspector of Ding Province; enfeoffed Duke of Zhao state with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: " Du Guxin's father Kuzhe was posthumously made bearer of the staff, grand commandant, superior pillar of state, director of military affairs in Ding, Heng, Cang, Ying, Ping, and Yan provinces, and inspector of Ding Province; he was enfeoffed Duke of Zhao with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Gong (Respectful).

sentences.zh: 信母費連氏，贈太尉恭公夫人。

translations.literal: Du Guxin's mother, Lady Feilian, was posthumously made Lady of Grand Commandant Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin's mother, Lady Feilian, was posthumously made Lady of Grand Commandant Gong.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳崇字尚樂，代郡武川人。

translations.literal: Houmo Chencheng, styled Shangle, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Houmo Chencheng, styled Shangle, came from Wuchuan in Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先，魏之別部，居庫斛真水。

translations.literal: His forebears were a separate branch of Wei, dwelling at Kuhuzhen River.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was a separate branch of the Wei people, settled on the Kuhuzhen River.

sentences.zh: 五世祖曰太骨都侯。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was titled Marquis Taigudu.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor was titled Marquis Taigudu.

sentences.zh: 其後，世為渠帥。

translations.literal: Thereafter for generations they were tribal chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter for generations they served as tribal chiefs.

sentences.zh: 祖允，以良家子鎮武川，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun, as a respectable household son, garrisoned Wuchuan and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun, posted to Wuchuan as a respectable household soldier, settled his family there.

sentences.zh: 父興，殿中將軍、羽林監。

translations.literal: His father Xing was a palace guard general and supervisor of the Forest of Wings guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xing was a palace guard general and supervisor of the Forest of Wings guard.

sentences.zh: 崇少驍勇，善馳射，謹愨少言。

translations.literal: Chencheng from youth was fierce and brave, skilled at mounted archery, careful and taciturn.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chencheng was fierce and brave, skilled at mounted archery, careful and sparing of speech.

sentences.zh: 年十五，隨賀拔岳與爾朱榮征葛榮。

translations.literal: At fifteen he followed Heba Yue with Erzhu Rong against Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he followed Heba Yue with Erzhu Rong against Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 又從元天穆討邢杲，平之。

translations.literal: Again he followed Yuan Tianmu against Xing Gao and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Yuan Tianmu against Xing Gao and crushed the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以功除建威將軍。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 別從岳破元顥於洛陽。

translations.literal: Separately following Yue he defeated Yuan Hao at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On a separate command under Heba Yue he defeated Yuan Hao at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遷直寢。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Attendant of the Inner Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to direct attendant of the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 後從岳入關，破赤水蜀。

translations.literal: Later following Yue into the Pass he broke the Chishui Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Heba Yue through the Pass, he broke the Chishui Shu.

sentences.zh: 時万俟醜奴圍岐州，遣其將李。

translations.literal: At that time Wanqi Chounu besieged Qi Province and dispatched his general Li.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wanqi Chounu besieged Qi Province and dispatched a general, Li.

sentences.zh: 尉遲菩薩將兵向武功。

translations.literal: Yuchi Pusa led troops toward Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Pusa led troops toward Wugong.

sentences.zh: 崇從岳力戰破之，乘勝逐北，解岐州圍。

translations.literal: Chencheng followed Yue in fierce battle, broke them, pursued north in victory, and lifted the siege of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chencheng followed Heba Yue in hard fighting, routed the enemy, pursued the fleeing force, and lifted the siege of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 又赴百里細川，破賊帥侯伏侯元進柵。

translations.literal: Again he went to Baili Xichuan and broke the stockade of the bandit chief Houfu Hou Yuanjin.
translations.idiomatic: He again went to Baili Xichuan and broke the stockade of the rebel chief Houfu Hou Yuanjin.

sentences.zh: 醜奴率其餘衆奔高平，崇與輕騎逐北，至涇州長坑及之。

translations.literal: Chounu led the remnant masses in flight to Gaoping; Chencheng with light cavalry pursued north and caught them at Changkeng in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chounu led the remnant host in flight toward Gaoping; Chencheng with light cavalry pursued north and caught them at Changkeng in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 賊未成列，崇單騎入賊中，於馬上生擒醜奴。

translations.literal: Before the rebels could form ranks, Chencheng alone rode into their midst and captured Chounu alive from horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rebels could form ranks, Chencheng rode alone into their midst and captured Chounu alive from horseback.

sentences.zh: 於是大呼，衆悉披靡，莫敢當之。

translations.literal: Then he gave a great shout; all collapsed before him, none daring to stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: Then he gave a great shout; the enemy ranks collapsed, and none dared stand against him.

sentences.zh: 後騎益集，賊徒因悉逃散，遂大破之。

translations.literal: Rear horsemen gathered ever more; the rebel band therefore all fled and scattered, and he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: More horsemen kept gathering behind him; the rebels therefore broke and scattered, and he won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 岳以醜奴所乘馬及寶劍金帶賞崇。

translations.literal: Yue rewarded Chencheng with the horse Chounu had ridden and a treasured sword with golden belt.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue rewarded Chencheng with Chounu's own horse and a treasured sword with golden belt.

sentences.zh: 除安北將軍、太中大夫、都督，封臨涇縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pacifying-the-North General, Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Commander; enfeoffed Marquis of Linjing county with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made pacifying-the-north general, palace attendant-in-ordinary, and commander, and enfeoffed Marquis of Linjing with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及岳為侯莫陳悅所害，崇與諸將同謀迎太祖。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Chencheng with the other generals jointly plotted to welcome Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue was murdered by Houmochen Yue, Chencheng and the other generals jointly planned to welcome Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 太祖至軍，原州刺史史歸猶為悅守。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor reached the army, Governor Shi Gui of Yuan Province still held the city for Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai reached the army, Shi Gui, governor of Yuan Province, still held the city for Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣崇襲歸。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor dispatched Chencheng to strike Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai dispatched Chencheng to strike Shi Gui.

sentences.zh: 崇潛軍夜往，輕將七騎，直到城下，餘衆皆伏於近路。

translations.literal: Chencheng moved his army by night in secret; with seven light horsemen he went straight to the wall; the rest all lay in ambush on the nearby road.
translations.idiomatic: Chencheng moved by night in secret; with seven light horsemen he went straight to the wall while the rest lay in ambush on the nearby roads.

sentences.zh: 歸見騎少，遂不設備。

translations.literal: Gui saw the horsemen were few and therefore made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gui saw the horsemen were few and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 崇卽入據城門。

translations.literal: Chencheng at once entered and seized the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chencheng at once entered and seized the gate.

sentences.zh: 時李遠兄弟在城內，先知崇來，於是中外鼓噪，伏兵悉起，遂擒歸，斬之以崇行原州事。

translations.literal: At that time Li Yuan and his brothers were inside the city, having foreknown Chencheng's coming; thereupon within and without they raised a clamor, ambush troops all sprang up, and they captured Gui and beheaded him; Chencheng acted as governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan and his brothers were inside the city and had foreknown Chencheng's approach; thereupon they raised a clamor within and without, ambush troops sprang up everywhere, and they captured and beheaded Shi Gui; Chencheng then acted as governor of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 仍從平悅，轉征西將軍。

translations.literal: Still following in pacifying Yue, he was transferred to Campaigning-in-the-West General.
translations.idiomatic: Still following in the campaign against Houmochen Yue, he was transferred to campaigning-in-the-west general.

sentences.zh: 又遣崇慰撫秦州，別封廣武縣伯，邑七百戶。

translations.literal: Again Chencheng was sent to reassure and settle Qin Province; separately enfeoffed Baron of Guangwu county with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Chencheng was again sent to reassure and settle Qin Province and was separately enfeoffed Baron of Guangwu with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，除涇州刺史，加散騎常侍、大都督，進爵為公，累遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，改封彭城郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was appointed Governor of Jing Province, added Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and Grand Commander, advanced in rank to Duke, and successively promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal-in-Protocol to the Three Ministers, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, and Opener-of-Office Equal-in-Protocol to the Three Ministers; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Pengcheng commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong (535) he was made governor of Jing Province, given scattered-cavalry regular attendant and grand commander, advanced to duke, and successively promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-in-protocol to the three ministers, grand general of fast cavalry, and opener-of-office equal in rank to the three ministers; his title was changed to Duke of Pengcheng with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 三年，從擒竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shayuan; his fief was increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shayuan; his fief was increased by two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 四年，從戰河橋，崇功居多。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed in battle at Heqiao; Chencheng's merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed in the battle at Heqiao; Chencheng's merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 七年，稽胡反，崇率衆討平之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Ji Hu rebelled; Chencheng led troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Ji Hu rebelled; Chencheng led troops and put the rebellion down.

sentences.zh: 尋除雍州刺史，兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yong Province and concurrently Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made governor of Yong Province and concurrently tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十五年，進位柱國大將軍，轉少傅。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he advanced to the rank of Pillar Grand General and was transferred to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was advanced to pillar grand general and transferred to junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，出為寧州刺史，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he went out as Governor of Ning Province and was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei (554) he went out as governor of Ning Province and was transferred to director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜大司空。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進封梁國公，邑萬戶，加太保。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Liang state with a fief of ten thousand households and added Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Liang with a fief of ten thousand households and made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 歷大宗伯、大司徒。

translations.literal: He held successively Grand Minister of Ritual and Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as grand minister of ritual and grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，崇從高祖幸原州，高祖夜還京師，竊怪其故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, Chencheng followed High Ancestor on a visit to Yuan Province; High Ancestor returned to the capital by night, privately wondering at the reason.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding (563), Chencheng followed High Ancestor Yuwen Yong on a visit to Yuan Province; Yuwen Yong returned to the capital by night, privately wondering at the reason.

sentences.zh: 崇謂所親人常昇曰：「吾昔聞卜筮者言，晉公今年不利。

translations.literal: Chencheng told his intimate Chang Sheng: "I once heard diviners say the Duke of Jin will have ill fortune this year.
translations.idiomatic: Chencheng told his confidant Chang Sheng: "I once heard diviners say the Duke of Jin will meet ill fortune this year.

sentences.zh: 車駕今忽夜還，不過是晉公死耳。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage now suddenly returns by night—nothing but that the Duke of Jin will die.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage now suddenly returns by night—nothing but that the Duke of Jin will die."

sentences.zh: 」於是衆皆傳之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon all transmitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the remark spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 或有發其事者。

translations.literal: Someone reported the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 高祖召諸公卿於大德殿，責崇。

translations.literal: High Ancestor summoned the lords and ministers to Dade Hall and reproached Chencheng.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong summoned the lords and ministers to Dade Hall and rebuked Chencheng.

sentences.zh: 崇惶恐謝罪。

translations.literal: Chencheng fearfully begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Chencheng fearfully begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 其夜，護遣使將兵就崇宅，逼令自殺。

translations.literal: That night Hu sent envoys with troops to Chencheng's residence and forced him to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yuwen Hu sent envoys with troops to Chencheng's residence and forced him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 禮葬如常儀。

translations.literal: He was buried with full ritual as usual.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried with the usual full rites.

sentences.zh: 諡曰躁。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zao.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zao (Restless).

sentences.zh: 護誅後，改諡曰莊閔。

translations.literal: After Hu was executed, the posthumous title was changed to Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Hu was executed, his posthumous title was changed to Zhuangmin (Solemn and Lamented).

sentences.zh: 子芮嗣。

translations.literal: His son Rui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui succeeded.

sentences.zh: 拜大將軍，進位柱國。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General and advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand general and advanced to pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 從高祖東伐，率衆守太行道。

translations.literal: Following High Ancestor's eastern campaign, he led troops to guard the Taihang route.
translations.idiomatic: Following High Ancestor Yuwen Yong's eastern campaign, he led troops to guard the Taihang route.

sentences.zh: 幷州平，授上柱國。

translations.literal: When Bing Province was pacified, he was granted Superior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing Province was pacified, he was granted superior pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 仍從平鄴，拜大司馬。

translations.literal: Still following in pacifying Ye, he was appointed Grand Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Still following in the pacification of Ye, he was appointed grand minister of war.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：蕭何文吏自愛，懼秦法誅戮，乃推奉漢高；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xiao He, a literate clerk who cherished himself, feared Qin law's execution and punishment, and thereupon promoted and supported Han Gaozu;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Xiao He, a literate clerk who prized his own safety, feared Qin law's punishments and thereupon raised up Han Gaozu;

sentences.zh: 李通家傳讖術，知劉氏當興，遂翊戴光武。

translations.literal: Li Tong's family transmitted prognostic arts, knew the Liu clan would rise, and thereupon assisted and supported Emperor Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong's family handed down prognostic arts, knew the Liu house would rise, and thereupon supported Emperor Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 終而白水復禹，中陽纂堯。

translations.literal: In the end Baishui restored Yu; Zhongyang succeeded Yao.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Liu Xiu restored the Han line at Baishui, and the throne passed as from Yao to Shun at Zhongyang.

sentences.zh: 方策以為美談，功臣仰其徽烈。

translations.literal: Historical records took it as fine talk; meritorious ministers looked up to their eminence and glory.
translations.idiomatic: Historical records treat them as exemplary tales; later ministers look up to their eminence and glory.

sentences.zh: 趙貴志懷忠義，首倡大謀，爰啟聖明，克復讐恥。

translations.literal: Zhao Gui's will harbored loyalty and righteousness, first initiated the great plan, thereby opened the sage brightness, and recovered revenge and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui was loyal at heart, first to raise the great design, helped open the way to sage rule, and avenged national dishonor.

sentences.zh: 關中全百二之險，周室定三分之業，彼此一時，足為連類。

translations.literal: Guanzhong held the hundred-and-two strategic passes; the Zhou house fixed the three-part enterprise—they were of the same age, fully worthy of parallel classification.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong held the hundred-and-two strategic passes; the Zhou house fixed the three-part enterprise—they belong to the same age and are fully worthy of comparison.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信威申南服，化洽西州。

translations.literal: Du Guxin's authority extended over the southern domains; his influence harmonized the Western Province.
translations.idiomatic: Du Guxin's authority reached the southern domains; his influence harmonized the western provinces.

sentences.zh: 信著遐方，光照鄰國。

translations.literal: His trustworthiness was famed in distant regions; his brilliance shone on neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: His trustworthiness was famed in distant lands; his brilliance shone on neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳崇以勇悍之氣，當戰爭之利，輕騎啟高平之扉，疋馬得長坑之捷。
